chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Jameel ibn Darraj and Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Bukayr and Ja'far ibn Sama'a from Ibn Bukayr and Jameel, all of them from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The first blood she sees from the third menstruation, so she is irrevocably divorced from him.
ai.seo_question: When does a woman's divorce become irrevocably final according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'iddah expiration by linking the irrevocability of divorce (ba'in) to the observation of the third menstrual cycle, a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for determining when a woman is free to remarry. It underscores the importance of physical signs in establishing legal status, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to family law. This ruling ensures clarity in marital transitions, preventing ambiguity in the woman's eligibility for a new marriage contract.
